summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with a history of psoriatic arthritis on immunosuppressive therapy was admitted for a severe joint pain flare affecting multiple left-sided joints, beginning in the shoulder and spreading overnight. The flare was attributed to recent tapering of prednisone and discontinuation of azathioprine. Evaluation showed no signs of infection in the joints or prior left leg fluid collections, with stable imaging and negative cultures. The patient was treated with an increase in prednisone to 40 mg daily, rotation from hydromorphone to oxycodone for better pain control, and uptitration of gabapentin and lidocaine patches. Pain improved significantly, and the patient remained afebrile and stable. A minor fall during admission prompted a head CT, which showed no acute abnormalities. He was discharged home with optimized pain and arthritis management, instructions to follow up with rheumatology, and guidance on monitoring for infection or worsening symptoms.
